note: FRANK-§0. Generated from the specification. Spec-derived fields are overwritten on every run; owner/implementation/test/threshold/evidence/status are human-maintained and merged forward by record id. Run `pnpm registry:generate` after editing the spec.

records.title: Users, trust zones, and deployment intent
Route and screen contracts
records.test: apps/api/src/test/api-contract.test.ts :: "FRANK-§3.8 authorization never trusts the client route"

records.text: Today must combine calendar, tasks, goals, routines, waiting items, messages, agent work, and system exceptions into one prioritised view.
records.acceptance: Fixture account produces a deterministic brief with links to every source record.
records.test: apps/api/src/test/api-contract.test.ts :: "UX-001 (partial) today" (Slice 1 subset; `coverage` declares the inputs later slices supply)

records.text: FRANK must generate morning and evening briefs and regenerate them on demand.
records.acceptance: Scheduled and manual runs produce equivalent cited outputs and record inputs.

records.text: Universal capture must accept text, voice, images, documents, URLs, and forwarded content.
records.acceptance: Each input type creates an immutable source envelope and a triage item.
records.test: apps/api/src/test/slice1.integration.test.ts :: "UX-003 — replaying a capture produces one source and one work item" (text and voice only in Slice 1)

records.text: Capture must acknowledge durability in under 500 ms at the API boundary, even when downstream enrichment is delayed.
records.acceptance: Load test and queue interruption test.
records.test: apps/api/src/test/capture-latency.test.ts (queue interruption) and apps/api/src/test/slice1.integration.test.ts :: "UX-004 — durability acknowledged in under 500 ms" (real PostgreSQL)

records.text: Steven must be able to say “remember,” “do,” “build,” “research,” “schedule,” or “send” without selecting a technical agent.
records.acceptance: Intent routing eval passes representative natural-language commands.

records.text: Every recommendation must be dismissible, explainable, and trainable through simple feedback.
records.acceptance: Feedback changes ranking without erasing the original event.

records.text: The interface must show stale data and sync failures rather than silently presenting an old state as current.
records.acceptance: Connector outage test displays age and recovery action.
records.test: apps/api/src/test/api-contract.test.ts :: "UX-007: every non-healthy component carries its age and a recovery action"

records.text: Important work must remain findable by outcome, person, project, topic, source, or date.
records.acceptance: Search acceptance set meets retrieval targets in section 20.

records.text: Tasks, goals, calendar commitments, messages requiring action, app issues, and automation exceptions must share a common `WorkItem` contract.
records.acceptance: Cross-domain query returns a consistent state and ownership model.

records.text: A work item must support owner, collaborators, status, priority, dates, dependencies, context, source, policy, artifacts, and history.
records.acceptance: Contract and migration tests cover every field and transition.

records.text: Work can be delegated to a person, agent profile, team of agents, or external system without changing its identity.
records.acceptance: Reassignment retains history, evidence, and dependency links.

records.text: Waiting, blocked, scheduled, active, reviewing, completed, cancelled, and failed states must be explicit.
records.acceptance: Invalid transitions are rejected and valid transitions are audited.
records.test: apps/api/src/test/slice1.integration.test.ts :: "WORK-004 — transitions through the API and the database"

records.text: Repeating work must use recurrence rules and idempotency keys, not copied ad hoc tasks.
records.acceptance: Retry and daylight-saving tests produce one intended occurrence.

records.text: All work must expose “why now,” “definition of done,” and “next safe action.”
records.acceptance: UI and API contract tests.
records.test: apps/api/src/test/api-contract.test.ts :: "exposes why now, definition of done, and next safe action on every item"

records.text: FRANK must synchronise selected calendars bidirectionally and preserve provider identifiers, recurrence, timezone, attendees, and change tokens.
records.acceptance: Round-trip, conflict, recurrence, and timezone suites pass.

records.text: Calendar planning must detect collisions, travel buffers, focus time, deadlines, and over-commitment.
records.acceptance: Scenario suite returns expected warnings and alternatives.

records.text: Email must support unified inbox, threads, labels/folders, attachments, semantic search, drafting, scheduled send, and follow-up tracking.
records.acceptance: Provider contract tests and evidence of source message lineage.

records.text: Untrusted message content must never directly authorize tools or disclose secrets.
records.acceptance: Prompt-injection test corpus cannot cross the execution boundary.
records.test: packages/policy/src/conformance/mandatory.test.ts :: "conformance 5/8 — confused-deputy" and apps/api/src/test/api-contract.test.ts :: "stores hostile content without letting it authorize anything"

records.text: Contact records must join identities across email, phone, calendar, X, organisations, and user-confirmed aliases.
records.acceptance: Merge/split tests preserve provenance and undo.

records.text: Meeting preparation must assemble relevant people, history, open work, documents, and suggested questions with citations.
records.acceptance: Representative meeting pack matches known evidence.

records.text: Meeting follow-up must produce notes, decisions, tasks, and draft messages, each linked to transcript or user notes.
records.acceptance: Source-linked outputs and correction flow demonstrated.

records.text: Outbound communication must obey per-channel standing policy and show the exact sent content in audit.
records.acceptance: Policy matrix tests draft, schedule, send, cancel, and retry paths.

records.title: Goals, habits, health, home, travel, and personal administration

records.text: Goals must support outcomes, measures, target dates, projects, habits, reviews, and evidence of progress.
records.acceptance: Goal roll-up derives progress from linked records and allows correction.

records.text: Habits and routines must support schedules, streaks, skips, notes, reminders, and trend summaries without punitive design.
records.acceptance: Recurrence and timezone tests; accessible mobile interaction.

records.text: Health data must be separately classified, consented, encrypted, and excluded from opportunistic model routes.
records.acceptance: Data-flow test proves only allowed processors receive health context.

records.text: FRANK may organise symptoms, appointments, medications, measurements, questions, and documents, but it must never diagnose or alter treatment. Informational output is labelled, and urgent-risk guidance follows a versioned clinician-reviewed red-flag policy and Steven's current location.
records.acceptance: No missed red-flag case in the hidden safety suite; every health response passes advice-boundary and source tests.

records.text: Home administration must track assets, warranties, maintenance, bills, providers, documents, and recurring obligations.
records.acceptance: Warranty-to-reminder and maintenance-history scenarios pass.

records.text: Travel planning must combine itinerary, bookings, documents, calendar, tasks, weather, local time, and disruption monitoring.
records.acceptance: Simulated trip generates a cited, timezone-correct travel pack.

records.text: Personal projects must use the same work, file, conversation, and automation contracts as software projects.
records.acceptance: Project switch retains consistent navigation and permissions.

records.text: Family or child-related data must support separate privacy and retention policies.
records.acceptance: Retrieval and export tests respect subject-level boundaries.

records.text: FRANK must ingest statements, receipts, invoices, subscriptions, bills, and user-entered transactions with source provenance.
records.acceptance: Sample corpus reconciles every extracted value to a source region.

records.text: Monetary values must use currency plus integer minor units or fixed-precision decimal; floating point is forbidden.
records.acceptance: Schema lint and arithmetic test suite.

records.text: Categories, merchants, accounts, tax labels, and reconciliation corrections must be versioned and reversible.
records.acceptance: Reclassification does not mutate the source and can be undone.

records.text: FRANK must detect renewals, unusual changes, duplicate charges, missing documents, and upcoming cash obligations.
records.acceptance: Known-anomaly fixture suite meets precision target.

records.text: Reports must distinguish recorded facts, estimates, and model-generated suggestions.
records.acceptance: UI/API snapshot tests show labels and confidence.

records.text: Moving money, opening accounts, accepting financial terms, or placing trades requires a separately enabled high-consequence connector policy.
records.acceptance: Default-deny integration tests.

records.text: Every ingested item must begin as a source envelope containing origin, author, capture method, timestamps, content hash, rights metadata, trust class, and raw artifact pointer.
records.acceptance: Ingestion contract rejects incomplete envelopes.

records.text: Raw sources must be immutable; corrections create new assertions, annotations, or tombstones.
records.acceptance: Correction test retains original and updates retrieval.

records.text: FRANK must support exact text, metadata, semantic, temporal, entity, and relationship search.
records.acceptance: Golden retrieval set measures each mode and hybrid ranking.

records.text: Answers from the brain must cite sources at passage or timestamp level and expose the retrieval path.
records.acceptance: Citation verifier confirms each cited span exists.

records.text: Facts must support valid-from, valid-to, observed-at, confidence, source, and supersession.
records.acceptance: Changing-address and changing-role scenarios return the right fact for a date.

records.text: Personal preference memories must be reviewable, editable, expirable, and deletable.
records.acceptance: Memory control screen and end-to-end deletion test.

records.text: Derived embeddings, summaries, entities, and graphs must be rebuildable from canonical sources.
records.acceptance: Projection deletion and full rebuild preserve source coverage, citation integrity, accepted assertions, authorization, and retrieval metrics within the registered tolerance for the projection revision.

records.text: Contradictory sources must remain visible; FRANK must not silently collapse them into one false certainty.
records.acceptance: Contradiction fixture returns both claims and an uncertainty record.

records.text: Knowledge scopes must include private, project, room, person, topic, and later customer cell.
records.acceptance: Cross-scope leakage tests return zero unauthorized results.

records.text: Export must produce human-readable files plus machine-readable source, assertion, link, and provenance records.
records.acceptance: Restore into an empty test cell recreates the selected knowledge set.

records.text: Connected X bookmarks must be captured through an official API where available, with an explicit browser-assisted fallback.
records.acceptance: Both adapters produce the same normalized source contract.

records.text: A bookmark must preserve post text, author, thread context, URLs, media pointers, timestamps, and capture time.
records.acceptance: Fixture thread generates complete envelope and media manifest.

records.text: FRANK must classify the item, extract claims and useful actions, find related knowledge, and propose a destination.
records.acceptance: Evaluation set meets classification and duplicate-detection targets.

records.text: Public posts are untrusted content and cannot issue system instructions.
records.acceptance: Adversarial-post corpus cannot trigger tools or retrieve secrets.

records.text: Bookmark removal or source deletion must support a user-selected keep, archive, or erase policy.
records.acceptance: Sync test applies each policy predictably.

records.text: Historical viewing may be imported from a user-provided export; continuous capture uses an opted-in browser extension because the public API does not provide complete watch history.
records.acceptance: Import and browser-capture fixtures deduplicate the same video.

records.text: Capture must record video ID, channel, title, URL, watch time, watched portion where observable, and the capture mechanism.
records.acceptance: Event schema and privacy UI tests.

records.text: Kid-oriented or family-background viewing must be excluded by default using account/profile, channel rules, title/topic signals, watch context, and user feedback.
records.acceptance: Labelled evaluation set reports precision, recall, and override behaviour.

records.text: Transcript acquisition must prefer creator captions, preserve language and timestamps, and clearly label generated transcription.
records.acceptance: Multiple transcript sources normalize without losing timestamps.

records.text: Each accepted video must create a wiki record with synopsis, chapter map, claims, examples, tools, people, action ideas, related knowledge, and timestamp citations.
records.acceptance: Golden-video set passes structural and citation checks.

records.text: A video without a transcript must remain a source record and may be queued for local or approved speech-to-text processing.
records.acceptance: No-transcript scenario remains searchable and resumable.

records.text: Copyrighted content must be stored and displayed according to user rights and source terms; summaries must not become unauthorised republication.
records.acceptance: Rights metadata and export policy tests.

records.title: Notes, bookmarks, media, voice, and notifications

records.text: Notes must support plain text and Markdown, folders, tags, wiki links, backlinks, attachments, daily notes, templates, source citations, and version history.
records.acceptance: Edit, conflict, backlink, attachment, export, and restore scenarios pass.

records.text: A generated note must remain distinguishable from a source, an accepted fact, and Steven's own writing.
records.acceptance: UI and API expose authorship, source, and confirmation state.

records.text: Notes may propose tasks, people, decisions, events, and memories, but extraction may not silently mutate those domains.
records.acceptance: Proposal and acceptance audit is complete.

records.text: General bookmarks must preserve URL, resolved URL, title, author, snapshot, selected text, note, tags, collection, source time, capture time, and availability state.
records.acceptance: Redirect, duplicate, deleted-page, and archived-snapshot tests pass.

records.text: FRANK must detect duplicates and syndicated copies without losing each capture's provenance or note.
records.acceptance: Duplicate corpus groups related items while preserving originals.

records.text: Studio must manage images, audio, video, documents, source files, generated variants, previews, rights, prompts, models, edits, and publication history.
records.acceptance: Asset lineage can reproduce or explain every generated output.

records.text: Image, speech, music, video, document, HyperFrames, and CAD capabilities must be separate provider or worker modules.
records.acceptance: Each module can be disabled or replaced without breaking the asset library.

records.text: Media generation must retain content credentials, rights and consent metadata where applicable and prevent private inputs from entering ineligible providers.
records.acceptance: Provider-route and publication checks pass.

records.text: Voice capture must provide transcript preview, language, confidence, correction, and a retained audio policy before creating work.
records.acceptance: Mobile and desktop voice journeys pass with offline retry.

records.text: Spoken responses must be optional, interruptible, privacy-aware, and paired with equivalent text.
records.acceptance: Accessibility and private-setting tests pass.

records.text: Notifications must support in-app, web push, email, and optional ntfy-compatible channels with priority, quiet hours, deduplication, escalation, deep links, and delivery receipts.
records.acceptance: Retry and provider-outage tests produce no notification storms.

records.text: A notification must explain the outcome or action needed; routine technical activity belongs in the timeline, not as an interruption.
records.acceptance: Notification quality fixture set passes plain-language and urgency rules.

records.text: FRANK must monitor a curated registry of official research, product, security, release, standards, and pricing sources.
records.acceptance: Daily run records fetch state, source health, and new items.

records.text: Sources must use RSS, release feeds, APIs, sitemaps, or polite page checks with conditional requests and rate limits.
records.acceptance: Network test verifies caching, backoff, and terms metadata.

records.text: Every finding must be deduplicated, trust-labelled, summarised, and mapped to affected requirements, modules, ADRs, or evals.
records.acceptance: Known release note creates the expected impact record.

records.text: FRANK must distinguish information, a candidate, a tested improvement, and an accepted product change.
records.acceptance: State transition tests prevent direct source-to-production promotion.

records.text: When a finding warrants code, FRANK must prepare an isolated change with tests, cross-model review, preview, and evidence while Steven is away.
records.acceptance: Simulated overnight run ends at review-ready state with no production change.

records.text: Low-value churn must be suppressed using impact score, confidence, expected value, compatibility, operational cost, and change budget.
records.acceptance: Replay set shows stable rejection of cosmetic or duplicative updates.

records.text: Rejected candidates must retain a reason and reconsideration trigger.
records.acceptance: Candidate register supports future re-evaluation without duplicate work.

records.text: FRANK must check provider pricing, free-credit offers, rate limits, model access, expiry, geography, privacy terms, and reliability each day.
records.acceptance: Provider fixtures produce normalized offers and expiry alerts.

records.text: Offers must be verified from provider-controlled sources before routing real work.
records.acceptance: Unverified social post remains quarantined and cannot become a route.

records.text: Free or promotional capacity must be treated as opportunistic, expiring, and lower-trust until verified otherwise.
records.acceptance: Route policy refuses sensitive data and has an automatic fallback.

records.text: New capacity must pass authentication, health, capability, quality, privacy, and cost probes before activation.
records.acceptance: Failing probe cannot enter an active pool.

records.text: A public or shared key must never be stored in source control or used for private customer or sensitive personal data.
records.acceptance: Secret scanner and data-class route tests.

records.text: Deal value must be measured as cost per successful task at the required quality, not advertised token price alone.
records.acceptance: Dashboard reports eval-adjusted value and failure cost.

records.text: Every app must have a durable project record, product brief, architecture, requirements, repository, environments, owners, risks, and release history.
records.acceptance: Project completeness gate rejects missing authority records.

records.text: FRANK must turn an idea into research, specification, acceptance tests, dependency graph, issues, and a build-ready context pack.
records.acceptance: Reference idea produces all required artifacts with links.

records.text: Untrusted repositories and agent-written executable code must run in a disposable hardened microVM with declared tools, credentials, network policy, and resource limits. A Git worktree may organize a branch only inside that execution boundary; it is never the security boundary. Rootless containers are reserved for trusted, pinned first-party jobs.
records.acceptance: Malicious-repository escape, cleanup, and reproducibility tests.

records.text: Multiple harnesses and agents must be able to work on separate bounded tasks and exchange structured progress through FRANK and Buzz.
records.acceptance: Multi-agent integration test merges non-conflicting changes and detects conflicts.

records.text: FRANK must support repositories on the VPS, GitHub, and later additional forges through a forge adapter.
records.acceptance: Contract suite passes against local Git and GitHub test repositories.

records.text: All code changes must run formatting, lint, type, unit, integration, security, dependency, and relevant end-to-end checks.
records.acceptance: Required-check policy blocks incomplete evidence.

records.text: User-facing changes must produce a preview environment and visual comparison on desktop and mobile viewports.
records.acceptance: Evidence pack contains working URL, screenshots, and browser checks.

records.text: Database changes require forward migration, compatibility window, backup point, rollback or fix-forward procedure, and restore test.
records.acceptance: Migration rehearsal passes on production-shaped data.

records.text: FRANK must perform a fresh-context review and a cross-model-family review with severity and evidence requirements.
records.acceptance: Seeded critical defects are found; low-value comments remain below noise target.

records.text: Review agents must not share the implementing agent's hidden context or be told the desired verdict.
records.acceptance: Review harness test confirms isolated prompts and independent model route.

records.text: Binary tests and deterministic tools outrank model opinion.
records.acceptance: A favourable review cannot override a failing required check.

records.text: A completed change pack must be ready before Steven is asked to promote it.
records.acceptance: Review item contains code, checks, preview, risks, rollback, spend, and change summary.

records.text: Every production promotion must declare and implement one transaction mode: pre-commit cancellable, atomic artifact/traffic-pointer change, or post-commit compensating recovery. The selected mode, point of no return, health gates, and recovery action must be visible before promotion and assessed automatically afterward.
records.acceptance: Tests interrupt promotion before and after the declared commit point and verify the exact cancellation or recovery result.

records.text: Incidents must create a timeline, affected services, containment actions, evidence, recovery, and follow-up work.
records.acceptance: Failure exercise produces a complete incident record.

records.text: FRANK must support creating web apps, APIs, workers, automations, browser extensions, desktop shells, mobile web apps, documents, data pipelines, and optional media/CAD outputs through project templates.
records.acceptance: Template conformance suite and sample builds.

records.text: Agent-generated branches must not trigger privileged forge workflows or access production environments, deployment credentials, organization secrets, or unsafe ownership changes.
records.acceptance: A generated CI-change branch attempts seeded secret exfiltration and receives no privileged job or secret.

records.text: Buzz must provide private rooms where Steven and agents collaborate as first-class members.
records.acceptance: Steven and every enabled harness pass the common identity, membership, signed-event, job, replay, and revocation contract.

records.text: Each project, incident, substantial research topic, or long-running change may have a linked room.
records.acceptance: Creating a project provisions or links a room idempotently.

records.text: Buzz events must be signed and retained according to room policy.
records.acceptance: Signature and membership tests pass.

records.text: Buzz is not the canonical life database, build database, workflow engine, secret store, or compliance audit.
records.acceptance: Service boundaries and failure test prove FRANK remains authoritative.

records.text: Relevant room events must project into FRANK using explicit event mappings and provenance.
records.acceptance: Rebuild test recreates projections from retained signed events.

records.text: A Buzz outage must not lose canonical jobs or prevent FRANK from showing their state.
records.acceptance: Outage and replay test.

records.text: A Buzz message, reaction, or signed event is an untrusted collaboration proposal until a FRANK command resolves actor, membership-at-event-time, schema, artifact digest, replay state, and current policy. A Buzz event alone can never approve production or another consequential action.
records.acceptance: Revoked-key, replayed-event, altered-artifact, forged-reaction, and wrong-room tests all fail closed.

records.text: FRANK must reuse maintained Buzz components before building equivalent rooms, relay, ACP, CLI, agent, Git-event, Compose, or Helm functionality.
records.acceptance: Dependency inventory proves every custom overlap is removed, justified by an ADR, or upstreamed.

records.text: Production Buzz must run a tested pinned commit or immutable image while a separate canary tracks upstream `main` and runs compatibility, migration, security, and recovery checks daily.
records.acceptance: Canary report records upstream commit, changed contracts, test results, promotion decision, and rollback image.

records.text: `buzz-acp`, `buzz-agent`, `buzz-dev-mcp`, `buzz-cli`, custom ACP harness definitions, and native workflow actions may execute bounded work only through FRANK-issued assignments, capability grants, and receipts.
records.acceptance: A direct capability escalation, duplicate scheduler, missing receipt, or bypassed FRANK policy fails closed.

records.text: Buzz workflow actions are allowed for room-local, reversible collaboration tasks; Temporal remains the durable scheduler and completion authority for life administration, app builds, overnight work, retries, approvals, and consequential effects.
records.acceptance: Restart, duplicate-delivery, pending-input, and long-running tests preserve one canonical FRANK run and one effect receipt.

records.text: Buzz Git/NIP-34 features may provide branch rooms, event mirroring, and canary hosting, but the selected production forge remains authoritative until Buzz passes required forge, recovery, CI, protection, review, and migration tests.
records.acceptance: Bidirectional reference and disaster-recovery tests preserve commit identity without granting Buzz privileged deployment credentials.

records.text: Every model, media, hosting, storage, and paid connector cost must attach to a run, project, automation, and provider account where possible.
records.acceptance: Cost reconciliation reaches the target in section 20.

records.text: Budgets must exist per day, month, project, automation, agent, provider, and customer cell.
records.acceptance: Budget test reroutes, slows, or stops according to policy.

records.text: Steven must be able to pause a run, agent, connector, automation class, model provider, or the whole execution plane.
records.acceptance: Containment exercise meets time target.

records.text: Health must distinguish healthy, degraded, unavailable, stale, and intentionally paused.
records.acceptance: Fault injection maps each state correctly.

records.text: Backups must be encrypted, off-cell, monitored, and regularly restored into an isolated environment.
records.acceptance: Restore drill evidence and checksum comparison.

records.text: Upgrades must use pinned artifacts, compatibility checks, migration rehearsal, signed provenance, and rollback or fix-forward instructions.
records.acceptance: Supply-chain and upgrade rehearsal pass.
